correctness.rationale: In C_3 square C_n for odd n, a shortest cross-row path switches rows exactly once; its column motion is a unique shortest cycle arc. An inclusion-maximal visible set must occupy every row, otherwise a new vertex can be placed in the empty row and connect to all selected vertices without internal interference. For occupancy patterns (1,1,1) and (2,1,1), extension in a singleton/paired row yields a larger visible set: for the pair in one row, the third cycle point k+1 gives gaps d,k+1-d,k all <=k. The proposed five-set has ten pairwise witness geodesics and its six exhaustive external-vertex column cases produce blocked witness pairs. An independent BFS shortest-path obstruction computation verified the five-set is maximal for n=5 and 7 and exhaustively excluded all smaller maximal sets for those n. The all-odd-n theorem rests on the case proof, not extrapolated BFS.
